options.text: With the cell disconnected, end P is still a South pole and end Q is still a North pole.
End P is a North pole and end Q is a South pole.
End P is a South pole and end Q is a North pole.
Both ends P and Q are South poles.

stem:
The diagram shows Avni's electromagnet: a coil of insulated copper wire on an iron nail joined to a cell. Ends of the nail are labelled P and Q. A magnetic compass is held near end P; the north pole of the compass needle is attracted towards P.

Which claim about the poles is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Unlike poles attract, so the compass north pole moving toward P means P is South and Q, the opposite end, is North. The coil must be connected for these poles.
teacher.figure_note: Electromagnet coil on nail with cell; compass north attracted to end P.
